On Sat, Jul 15, 2017 at 7:19 PM, Jerin Kim <jrk...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Phil

I have two basic questions regarding the mirt package. I apologize it if these were already answered in the prior group discussions.
First, I wonder if guessing parameter can be estimated in polytomous models (extended from gpcm and grm) via mirt.

Do you have an IRT equation that reflects this guessing parameter? I'm not aware of such models, though they certainly could exist.
 
Second, I used D = 1.7 to re-calculate the thresholds at a RP of 2/3. Can I go with this scaling constant?

I'm not sure what this means, sorry.
 

I look forward to your answer.  Thanks,
Jerin

messages.author: ab237ff4f31a820f
messages.subject: Re: Questions
parts: If I'm not mistaken, Jerin's reference to RP 2/3 is regarding the commonly used "Response Probability" in standard setting (Bookmark method usually) to refer to the point at which an examinee theoretically has a 2 in 3 chance of answering correctly. This would not be accomplished by using the normal ogive conversion of 1.7 (or 1.702, http://demonstrations.wolfram.com/ComparingTheNormalOgiveAndLogisticItemCharacteristicCurves/). I don't have a ready link for something with a guessing parameter, but here's how to do the adjustment within a Rasch framework: http://raschforum.boards.net/thread/87/generating-rp67-winsteps

Hi,

I heard available to use RP .5 point when you set the standards with bookmark method even in the Rasch model perspective. RP 2/3 point is the just example I heard.

If you meant guess parameter of full credit, use 3PLNRM model.

In mirt parametrization, constraints to set a=1 when you called Rasch model.

Seongho

Hi,

I heard available to use RP .5 point when you set the standards with bookmark method even in the Rasch model perspective. RP 2/3 point is the just example I heard.

If you meant guess parameter of full credit, use 3PLNRM model.

That's true, you could use this itemtype (provided it achieves the sought-after modelling goal). To make this partial credit though the ak_k scoring coefficients would have to be fixed at 0,1,...,K-1, otherwise the default nominal response model behaviour is used. 

Phil

Thanks, all. 

I think I might need to explain my second question more clearly. I ran graded response model and got difficulties from coef(...,IRTpars=T). Then, I have tried to use the equation (theta = (1/Da)ln(x/(1-x)) + b (when RP = x, from Beretvas, 2004) so as to obtain the bookmark difficulty location for an RP of 2/3. I know, coef(…,IRTparts=T) produces a (discrimination) and b (difficulty). But I wonder if D (as a scaling constant) is 1.702 at this point.  As I read the prior post, I saw you answered 1 (to Dimitrios Zacharatos) . My understanding is...his question appears somewhat similar. 
Could you let me know what value can be used for the scaling constant D?

Thanks,

Jerin

Yes that's correct. So all coefs in mirt are on the logit scale, rather than the 1.7 adjusted logit scale to resemble the ogive metric.

Phil
